content.section_8.5_title: Management of pulmonary embolism in patients with cancer

evidence_summary.LMWH_vs_VKA: Five RCTs compared LMWH versus conventional VTE treatment (heparin followed by VKA) for cancer-associated thrombosis. Earlier trials reported a significant reduction in VTE recurrence with LMWH without increased bleeding; overall LMWHs decrease risk of recurrent VTE by ~40% with a similar risk of major bleeding compared with VKAs. LMWHs became the standard of care but are associated with cost and burden, and absolute recurrence while on LMWH remains higher in cancer patients (~7% reported) compared with non-cancer patients (~1.5–3%).
evidence_summary.NOACs_in_cancer: NOACs offer oral fixed-dose administration and potentially lower cost; however, only a small proportion (~3–9%) of patients in phase III NOAC VTE trials had concomitant cancer. A randomized open-label trial compared edoxaban with LMWH (dalteparin) in 1,050 patients with cancer-associated thrombosis. Edoxaban was started after 5 days of LMWH and given for 6 months. Edoxaban dosing: 60 mg once daily, reduced to 30 mg in subjects with moderate renal impairment, low body weight, or need for strong inhibitors of P‑glycoprotein. Edoxaban was non-inferior to dalteparin for prevention of VTE recurrence or major bleeding over 12 months (HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.70–1.36). Major bleeding occurred in 6.9% of edoxaban patients vs 4.0% in the dalteparin arm (difference ~2.9 percentage points).

practical_points: Assess and manage modifiable bleeding risk factors before deciding duration/regimen of anticoagulation.
Refer to supplementary tables for detailed therapeutic decision-making in specific clinical situations.
Do not reduce dabigatran or edoxaban dose for extended anticoagulation after PE unless supported by trial data; reduced-dose regimens were not investigated in extension trials.
LMWH remains recommended as standard treatment for cancer-associated VTE given trial evidence, but consider patient burden and cost.

When using edoxaban in cancer patients, follow dose-reduction criteria (renal impairment, low body weight, or interacting drugs) and note that therapy was initiated after at least 5 days of LMWH in the referenced trial.
